aria: Animated recap of the Timberwolves' 133 to 94 home win over the Mavericks: LaMelo Ball's 31-foot 3-pointer with 11:17 left in the third quarter that made it 70 to 53, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Ball's 22 points, 6 threes and 9 assists, the top scorers, how the Timberwolves won, and the next game at home against Chicago.
notes: Box score from the Timberwolves' 133–94 home win over the Dallas Mavericks at Target Center on Nov 12, 2026, from the Land of Basketball box score, checked against the FOX Sports box score and play-by-play, with game details from the Associated Press (via ABC News and WRAL) and the Dallas Sports Journal. All 133 Minnesota points and all 94 Dallas points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals (67–52 at the half and 103–69 after three, matching the AP). Team totals (field goals 52 of 90 to 35 of 94, threes 15 of 32 to 13 of 48, rebounds 50–38, assists 33–26) are from the box score. Minnesota's 44-point lead (129–85 with 2:47 left) and Dallas's 5-point lead (24–19 late in the first quarter) are read from the FOX Sports play-by-play; the AP also gives the 44. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Thursday's games: Minnesota 9–3 (third in the West), Dallas 7–5, Chicago 1–9.

Dallas led 20–16 late in the first quarter before Bones Hyland checked in; Minnesota outscored the Mavericks 18–6 the rest of the quarter (Dallas Sports Journal; FOX Sports play-by-play). Ball scored 16 points in the first half and 10 in the second quarter, sat all but 2:49 of the fourth, and finished with a season-high 9 assists (AP; Dallas Sports Journal). Ball and Hyland made 11 of 16 threes; the rest of the team made 4 of 16 (Dallas Sports Journal). Cooper Flagg, who scored 43 against Indiana in his previous game, was held to 12 (AP). It was Minnesota's fifth straight win, its most lopsided of the season and its seventh straight win over Dallas; it ended the Mavericks' three-game winning streak (AP). Anthony Edwards was inactive (box score). Minnesota hosts Chicago on Saturday, Nov 14 at 8:00 PM ET (the site's schedule; TickPick lists 7:00 PM Central at Target Center).

The play of the game is an original illustration of LaMelo Ball's 3-pointer from 31 feet, 43 seconds into the third quarter, assisted by Jonathan Kuminga, that made it 70–53 (FOX Sports play-by-play has it at 11:17 after a Flagg free throw made it 67–53; the Dallas Sports Journal gives the distance). It began a 17–4 run that made it 84–56, capped by Ball's alley-oop to Rudy Gobert (AP; FOX Sports play-by-play). The play-by-play calls it a jump shot; the recaps don't describe the move further, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Minnesota Timberwolves or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Ball’s listed 6-foot-7 and 180 pounds (RealGM), in Minnesota's home white with No. 1 (Heavy). No wingspan from a reliable measurement is reported, so his arms are drawn at a 1.0 ratio. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
